topic: Claude Code with a free local LLM: the Ollama setup
thesis: Claude Code was never married to Anthropic's cloud: because Ollama's local server speaks the Anthropic Messages API, three environment variables put a free model you already own behind the same terminal agent, if your context length and tool-calling hold up.
explanation_path: Start with what Claude Code actually is: a terminal client that sends Anthropic-format requests to whatever endpoint ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL names, which is why Claude Code's own docs describe the variable as changing where requests are sent, not which model answers them. Establish that Ollama implemented the Anthropic Messages API in v0.14.0, so a viewer's own machine can be that endpoint at http://localhost:11434. The connection itself is deliberately tiny: a dummy auth token, a blanked API key, the base URL -- or a single ollama launch claude line that sets all of it. Then come the two knobs that decide whether the redirect is worth anything. The model must be a real tool-caller: qwen3-coder:30b, a 19GB download that activates only 3.3B of its 30.5B parameters, or gpt-oss:20b, which its own page says runs on as little as 16GB of memory. And the server context must be raised, because Ollama's default on machines under 24 GiB VRAM is 4k tokens while its docs floor for agent and coding work is 64000. Once the setup works, the money lands: the same agent, zero per-prompt cost, no usage window. Close the loop with the honest catch: this is Ollama's engineering, not an Anthropic-supported path, and tool use is exactly where local models are weakest, so the honest promise is daily engineering work on your own box, not SWE-bench-scale refactors.

claims.claim: Ollama v0.14.0 and later answer the Anthropic Messages API, an ability announced January 16, 2026 that makes Claude Code drivable by open-source models.
claims.source_title: Claude Code with Anthropic API compatibility · Ollama Blog

claims.claim: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL changes where Claude Code's requests are sent, not which model answers them.
The official local setup is a dummy token, a blanked API key and the local base URL, then a model flag -- or the one-liner ollama launch claude.

Ollama defaults to a 4k context below 24 GiB VRAM (32k on 24-48 GiB, 256k at 48 GiB or more), its docs floor for agents and coding tools is at least 64000 tokens, and the server context is set with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve.
qwen3-coder:30b, Ollama's current-generation coding pick, is a 19GB download with a 256K context window: 30.5B parameters at Q4_K_M with only 3.3B activated, 11.4M downloads, Apache 2.0.
gpt-oss:20b is a 14GB download with 128K context whose own model page says it runs on systems with as little as 16GB memory, and its flagship sibling fits a single 80GB GPU.

Claude Code is unavailable on Anthropic's Free plan; the cheapest plan that includes it is Pro at $20 if billed monthly ($17 per month with annual subscription discount, $200 billed up front), and Max is $100 per month with 5x Pro usage every 5 hours and every week.
Anthropic's own quickstart lists a Claude subscription, a Console account, or a supported cloud provider as the prerequisite before you begin.
Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway, and while a gateway credential is active the subscription's usage limits do not apply to those requests.
claims.source_title: Other LLM gateways - Claude Code Docs

claims.claim: The gap that decides whether local works is agentic tool use, not chat quality: the previous-generation Gemma 3 27B scored 6.6% on the tau2-bench tool-use benchmark, a 4K context is exhausted in seconds and silently truncates files mid-edit, and malformed tool-call JSON loops on Invalid tool parameters.
claims.source_title: Local Agentic Programming on the Cheap: Claude Code + Ollama + Gemma4 - KDnuggets

analogy_candidates.vehicle: A courier route with a changeable drop-off address
analogy_candidates.mapping: Claude Code is the courier that always packs the same Anthropic-format boxes; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is only the delivery address, and Ollama is your garage that learned to sign for them.
analogy_candidates.limit: The receiving end had to implement the sender's exact protocol to sign at all, and once delivery is free the box quality depends on your garage's shelf space (VRAM), not the courier.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: A home gym versus the gym membership
analogy_candidates.mapping: Pro and Max are the all-inclusive gym whose front desk caps you every 5 hours and every week; the local model is the home gym with weights you already paid for (your GPU's memory) and no per-session fee.
analogy_candidates.limit: The workout spans many stations at once -- a large multi-file refactor -- where the gym's Opus-grade equipment still wins and your 30B home rack does not.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: An engine that fires only some cylinders
analogy_candidates.mapping: qwen3-coder:30b parks 30.5B parameters in the engine but burns only 3.3B per token, which is why a 30B model runs at all on a 24 GB card.
analogy_candidates.limit: The whole engine still has to sit in the garage -- the full 19GB of weights is in memory even when only a few cylinders fire.

misconceptions.myth: You need an Anthropic API key or paid account to point Claude Code at Ollama.
misconceptions.reality: The official local setup exports a dummy token, blanks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and talks to localhost; what you give up is Anthropic's endorsement and support, not a key (claim 3, claim 9).

misconceptions.myth: Any Ollama chat model can drive Claude Code.
misconceptions.reality: The model must call tools and hold context -- the docs floor for agent work is at least 64000 tokens and the old open model scored 6.6% on the tool-use benchmark (claim 4, claim 10).

misconceptions.myth: A 30B-parameter model needs roughly 30GB of memory.
misconceptions.reality: qwen3-coder:30b is 30.5B parameters but downloads as a 19GB file at Q4_K_M and activates only 3.3B per token (claim 5).

misconceptions.myth: Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and it just works.
misconceptions.reality: Out of the box Ollama serves a 4k context below 24 GiB VRAM, which an agentic session exhausts in seconds while silently truncating files mid-edit; raise OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH before judging the model (claim 4, claim 10).

glossary.definition: The unit a language model reads and writes in, roughly a short word or word fragment, and the unit context length is counted in.
The maximum number of tokens the model can hold in memory at once, per Ollama's docs "the maximum number of tokens that the model has access to in memory".
A named setting stored in your shell that programs read when they start, used here to redirect Claude Code's traffic.
The network address a client sends its API requests to; swapping Anthropic's server for localhost:11434 is the whole redirect.
The model's ability to request real actions (read a file, edit a file, run a command) instead of only producing text.
The suffix after the colon that picks a model variant and size, as in qwen3-coder:30b.
Storing weights at roughly 4 bits instead of 16, shrinking a 30.5B-parameter model to a 19GB file at a small quality cost.
An architecture where only a fraction of the total parameters fire for each token, so total size and per-token compute differ.
The subset of an MoE's weights used per token, e.g. only 3.3B of qwen3-coder:30b's 30.5B.
The memory on your graphics card, which decides how big a model and how large a context Ollama will run; a Mac's shared pool counts too ("memory or unified memory").
The extra memory the model needs on top of its weights to hold the conversation so far; it grows with context length and pages to disk when it outgrows memory.
A benchmark scoring how reliably a model calls tools, executes steps and handles errors across a multi-step agentic workflow -- exactly what Claude Code demands.

The claim that a 24 GB card fits qwen3-coder:30b with room for context is derived arithmetic from the 19GB file size, not a vendor statement; no Ollama-published table maps models to specific consumer GPUs.
No AMD- or Mac-specific performance guidance was fetched; memory-fit statements rest on Ollama's generic "memory or unified memory" wording.
Tokens per second on any specific machine has no number here; that is a first-party measurement for the build stage, not a web fact.
A Medium "reality check" article was unreachable (server 500 on two attempts) and contributed nothing to this brief.
suggested_outline:
Open on the meter: Pro is $20 a month, Max is $100 with caps every 5 hours, and the Free plan has no Claude Code at all.
Land the mechanism: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL changes where requests are sent, not which model answers them, and Ollama has spoken Anthropic's Messages API since v0.14.0.
Show the three lines: a dummy token, a blanked key, the local base URL -- or the single command ollama launch claude --model qwen3-coder.
Pick the model by hardware: qwen3-coder:30b is a 19GB download with only 3.3B parameters active per token; gpt-oss:20b runs on as little as 16GB.
Defuse the trap: Ollama's default context is 4k below 24 GiB VRAM while agent work wants at least 64000 tokens, so set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH before judging the model.
Close on the honest catch: Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models and tool use is where local models fall over (6.6% for the old open model on the tool-use benchmark), then the payoff: same terminal, same agent, zero dollars per prompt.
notes: Ran on web_search + web_extract with FireCrawl out of credits (402); 16 pages fetched across three research subagents plus one orchestrator fetch; the Micro Center walkthrough from the ideas note was intentionally not fetched so this brief stands on primary pages. Conflict to carry into the script: Anthropic's docs list a paid path as the prerequisite and disown routing Claude Code to non-Claude models (llm-gateway page), while Ollama publishes and maintains the integration as a feature of its own server; present the setup as Ollama's engineering, not Anthropic's blessing. Thin spots: no vendor statement that a 24 GB card fits qwen3-coder:30b (the 19GB file size is the verbatim fact); no tokens-per-second number exists until the build stage measures one; kimi-k2.7-code is cloud-only on Ollama ($0.95 input / $4.00 output per 1M tokens, 1.04T parameters), so it must not be presented as a free local option.
viewer_situation: You already use Claude Code on a Pro plan, or you have wanted a terminal coding agent, and a gaming PC or Mac with 16 to 24 GB of memory is sitting right there.
process_steps: Install Ollama and pull a tool-calling coding model sized to your memory (ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b for a 24 GB card, gpt-oss:20b for 16 GB).
Set the server context before serving: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve.

Point Claude Code at the local server: export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama, export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="", export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 -- or run ollama launch claude --model qwen3-coder.
Start Claude Code and run /status to confirm the connection.
objection: Anthropic does not support this path, and a local model that scores 6.6% on tool use will spend your evening emitting broken tool JSON -- the free prompts cost you the thing you were actually buying, an agent that finishes the job.
